core_obligations: Reduce to a single closed point (proof lines 11057-11060): since cohomology on a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme commutes with colimits, it suffices to show the vanishing of the cohomology of i_x of the constant sheaf Z for a single closed point x.

Compute the higher direct images (proof lines 11060-11065): the inclusion of a closed point is finite, so its higher direct images of the constant sheaf vanish in positive degrees, and the Leray spectral sequence identifies the cohomology of i_x of the constant sheaf with the cohomology of the constant sheaf on the point.
Conclude (proof lines 11065-11068): the point is the spectrum of an algebraically closed field, so its higher cohomology vanishes, which gives the statement.
proof_roadmap: Pass from the direct sum to a single closed point using commutation with colimits.
Use finiteness of the inclusion of a closed point and the Leray spectral sequence to reduce to the point.
Use the vanishing of the cohomology of the constant sheaf on the spectrum of an algebraically closed field.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the cohomology of the direct sum over the closed points of a smooth curve of the constant sheaf Z pushed forward from each point vanishes in positive degrees (statement lines 11051-11055, with the standing set-up delivered verbatim as a context span from lines 10937-10941). The proof reduces the direct sum to a single point through the commutation of cohomology with colimits (proof lines 11057-11060), uses that the inclusion of a closed point is finite and applies the Leray spectral sequence to identify the cohomology with that of the constant sheaf on the point (proof lines 11060-11065), and concludes by the vanishing on the spectrum of an algebraically closed field (proof lines 11065-11068). The non-formal content is the reduction to a single point. The claim is H2: three short steps, each written out.
